title: HSN Putrajaya 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: HSN Putrajaya Review: Start Times, Cut-offs, Prizes, Pack Collection
meta_description: HSN Putrajaya review from the 2025 race: a 4.30am half-marathon start at 24°C and 89% humidity, a 4-hour cut-off, RM65-120 entry, prize money five deep, and a messy race-kit collection.
dek: The Federal Territories' National Sports Day run in October 2025: when it started, how humid it was, what the 21 km cost and paid, what went wrong at race-kit collection, and what changes for 2026.
verdict: Enter if you live in the Klang Valley and want a cheap, local half marathon with a real chance of prize money. In 2025 the 21 km started at 4.30am on the Sunday with a four-hour cut-off, cost RM65 to RM90 for Malaysians, and paid cash five deep in every category. The catch is organisation. Race-kit collection in 2025 meant two-hour queues and shirts that had not arrived, and no route map or aid-station plan appeared on the registration pages. The air was also saturated, at 89% to 94% humidity. Collect your kit early, carry water, and expect the 2026 race to differ: the 21 km moves to Saturday at 5am.

sections.heading: What HSN Putrajaya Is
paragraphs: HSN Putrajaya is the Federal Territories' run for Hari Sukan Negara, Malaysia's National Sports Day, organised in 2025 by the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur's youth and sports department, Jabatan Belia dan Sukan WPKL [1][2]. The 2025 edition marked ten years of National Sports Day and ran over two days at Dataran Putrajaya in Presint 3: the 3 km family run and 5 km fun run on Saturday 11 October, and the 10 km and 21 km on Sunday 12 October [1][2].

The Saturday was a sports-day festival as much as a race. The government's Malaysia Aktif portal reported that about 6,200 people took part, that the Federal Territories minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa, flagged off the run, and that the programme included aerobics, traditional games, taekwondo, silambam, a climbing wall and an archery championship [3].

The Sunday races were competitive. The 21 km had Open, Malaysian (17 to 39) and Malaysian veteran (40 and over) categories for men and women; the 10 km was for Malaysians only [1]. It is a different race from HSN21km Putrajaya, a separate half marathon held a week later, on 19 October 2025, at Dataran Wawasan [4].

sections.heading: Start Times, Cut-offs and the Weather
paragraphs: The 21 km started at 4.30am with a four-hour cut-off, and the 10 km at 6.30am with two hours; the Saturday 3 km and 5 km started at 7.30am with 90 minutes [1]. One registration page listed the 10 km at 6.15am [2]; the organiser's own schedule graphic, posted later, says 6.30am [1].

Kuala Lumpur International Airport, about 21 km south of Dataran Putrajaya, recorded 24°C at 4.30am on race morning, with a dew point of 22°C, 89% humidity and a 4-knot wind [5]. The air grew wetter, not drier: from 6.30am to 8am it was 24°C with 94% humidity and almost no wind. By 8.30am, when the 21 km closed, it was 26°C with 84% humidity [5].

The temperature is mild, but at that humidity sweat barely evaporates, so a slower half marathoner finishing near the cut-off runs the whole race in saturated, still air. Carry water: no route map or aid-station plan appeared on either 2025 registration page [1][2].

sections.heading: Race-Kit Collection: What Went Wrong in 2025
paragraphs: Race kits were collected at Auditorium Tun Azizan Zainul in the Perbadanan Putrajaya complex on Friday 10 and Saturday 11 October. RaceXasia listed the hours as 11am to 7pm [2]; the organiser later posted updated hours of 11am to 10pm [1]. Runners had to bring their identity card or passport and their confirmation slip, or copies of both to collect for someone else [1].

It did not go smoothly. A participant posted, the day before the 5 km, that they had queued from 1.50pm and waited two hours, that not all the 5 km shirts had arrived, so some runners had to collect theirs on the morning of the race, and that the 21 km shirts had not arrived at all. They blamed both the department's secretariat and the shirt supplier, and asked for volunteers to check registrations by hand [6].
Entries cannot be refunded, transferred or deferred [7], so if you enter, plan to collect early.

sections.heading: Entry Fees, Prizes and Who It Suits
paragraphs: It was cheap. The 21 km cost RM65, RM75 or RM90 for Malaysians, depending on when you entered, and RM95 to RM120 in the Open category; the 10 km cost RM55 to RM70, and the 3 km and 5 km RM30 to RM60 [1].

The prize list goes deep. The 21 km Open paid RM900, RM700, RM600, RM500 and RM400 to the top five men and women; the Malaysian and veteran 21 km categories paid RM800 down to RM300, and the 10 km categories RM300 down to RM100. Places six to ten received a winner's medal but no cash [1]. Every finisher got a medal, and 21 km finishers also got a finisher tee [1][2].
Separate categories for Malaysians under and over 40, each paying five places, give a good local club runner several ways to win money.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you are based in the Klang Valley and want a low-cost, early-morning half marathon with prize money, or a family day out on the shorter distances. Think twice if you need a published course, a guaranteed smooth pack collection or cooler air.

The 2026 edition changes shape. It runs on 10 and 11 October 2026, with a new 30 km at 3.30am and the 21 km at 5am on the Saturday, and the 10 km at 6.30am and the 3 km and 5 km at 7.30am on the Sunday [8]. The cut-offs are six hours for the 30 km and four hours for the 21 km [8]. The 21 km costs up to RM100 for Malaysians and RM120 in the Open category, plus admin fee and insurance [8]. The 2026 event site says 3 km, 5 km and 10 km kits are collected a week before the race at MITEC Kuala Lumpur [9].
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's registration pages and graphics, a government sports portal report, a participant's post, and airport weather records.

faqs.question: What time does the HSN Putrajaya half marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2025 the 21 km started at 4.30am on Sunday 12 October, with the 10 km at 6.30am. For 2026 the 21 km moves to Saturday 10 October at 5am, after a new 30 km at 3.30am, and the 10 km, 5 km and 3 km run on Sunday 11 October.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off time for the HSN Putrajaya 21 km?
faqs.answer: Four hours, in both 2025 and 2026. The 10 km has two hours, the 5 km 90 minutes, and the new 30 km in 2026 has six hours. In 2025 the 21 km closed at 8.30am, when the nearest airport recorded 26°C and 84% humidity.

faqs.question: Is there prize money at HSN Putrajaya?
faqs.answer: Yes, five deep. In 2025 the 21 km Open paid RM900 to RM400 to the top five men and women, the Malaysian and veteran 21 km categories RM800 to RM300, and the 10 km categories RM300 to RM100. Sixth to tenth got a winner's medal without cash.

faqs.question: How humid is HSN Putrajaya on race morning?
faqs.answer: Very. At the 4.30am start in 2025 the nearest airport recorded 24°C, a dew point of 22°C and 89% humidity. From 6.30am to 8am humidity reached 94% with almost no wind. The temperature was mild, but sweat evaporates poorly in air that wet, so carry water.

faqs.question: Where do you collect the HSN Putrajaya race kit?
faqs.answer: In 2025 kits were collected at Auditorium Tun Azizan Zainul in the Perbadanan Putrajaya complex on the Friday and Saturday, with hours later extended to 10pm. A participant reported two-hour queues and missing shirts. For 2026, the event site says 3 km, 5 km and 10 km kits are collected at MITEC Kuala Lumpur.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the previous edition (11 and 12 October 2025). Material is thin: results (checkpointspot.asia) return HTTP 403 and were not read, and no route map, aid-station plan or runner's account of the Sunday races could be found, so the review is short. The 6,200 figure is the government portal's count for the Saturday programme, not the 21 km field. The 10 km start time differs between RaceXasia (6.15am) and the organiser's later graphic (6.30am); the graphic is used. The rules page gives older race-kit hours (8 to 10 October, to 6pm); the organiser's updated graphic (10 and 11 October, to 10pm) is used. Weather is from KLIA METAR observations, not a forecast. The participant who posted about race-kit collection is not named. No rating.
